column1: # Case table for substrate/.github/workflows/pleme-publish.yml
# TAB-separated: <name> <context k=v;k=v> <expect-run csv> <expect-skip csv>
# WHAT THIS WORKFLOW IS: a tier-2 fan-out. Five jobs, each a bare
# `inputs.target == '<name>'` equality, no `needs`, no toggle inputs, no
# `contains()`/`fromJSON()`. So the only axis is `target`, and the table gives
# it one row per arm plus the two boundary rows below.
# WHAT ROWS 1-5 PIN — MUTUAL EXCLUSION, and it is load-bearing rather than
# tidy. Every one of the five arms is a mutating publish path: action-release
# publishes an action, compliance-attest writes an attestation,
# npm-auto-release and python-auto-release publish packages, reusable-gen-spec
# commits a regenerated Cargo.gen.lock. Two arms selecting on one input would
# be a double-publish, so each row asserts its arm runs AND names all four
# others as skipped. Equality dispatch makes that structurally impossible
# today; the table is what keeps it impossible if a condition is ever widened
# (a `startsWith`, an `||`, a `contains`).
# WHAT ROWS 6-7 PIN — THAT THERE IS NO CATCH-ALL, and this is the row that
# matters most here. This workflow has no fallback job and no arm that fails
# an unrecognized target. Hand it a name it does not know and ALL FIVE JOBS
# SKIP, the workflow reports SUCCESS, and nothing at all was dispatched. That
# is precisely the shape that made graphql-synthesizer's green tick a lie on
# 2026-08-08: a deliberate skip and a broken skip render identically.
# The two rows do NOT assert that this is good. They assert it is the CURRENT
# behavior, so that (a) nobody reads a green run as evidence that something
# published, and (b) if someone later adds a guard job that fails on an
# unknown target, these two rows go red and they must consciously say so here
# rather than silently changing what a bad input does.
# Row 6 uses `cargo-ci` rather than a nonsense string on purpose. cargo-ci is
# a REAL reusable in the catalogue that is deliberately absent from this
# composer — the workflow's own header explains it nests, so it is dispatched
# straight from pleme.yml to stay inside GHA's 4-level cap. So `cargo-ci` is
# the plausible mistake, not a synthetic one: a caller reads the catalogue,
# routes a nesting reusable through the family composer, and is told SUCCESS.
# Row 7 is the distinct empty case — an upstream that computed a target and
# produced nothing (an unset matrix value, an expression resolving to ""),
# which is a different state from any named target and is exactly where a
# catch-all would be expected to earn its keep.
# `target` is `required: true`, which stops a caller OMITTING it. It does not
# stop a caller passing a wrong or empty one, so required-ness closes neither
# of these two rows.
action-release
compliance-attest
npm-auto-release
python-auto-release
reusable-gen-spec
# THE CATCH-ALL PROBE. A real-but-unrouted reusable name selects NOTHING and
# the run still reports success. Intended today; pinned so it stays a choice.
unknown-target-dispatches-NOTHING
# "Detect ran but produced nothing" — distinct from any named arm.
empty-target-dispatches-NOTHING
